content:lead-article.heading: Why Boise homeowners trust Peak Roofing Co
content:lead-article.subheading: Family-owned, GAF-certified, and built on 18 years of Treasure Valley roofs.
content:lead-article.lead: When a hailstorm rolls off the Boise Foothills, the difference between a quick patch and a lasting repair comes down to who is on your roof — and Peak Roofing Co has been the name Ada County families call first since 2007.
content:lead-article.body:
We started with a single truck and a simple promise: treat every roof like it was over our own family's heads. Today our crews replace and repair hundreds of roofs a year across Boise, Meridian, Eagle, and Nampa — and that promise hasn't changed.

Idaho weather is hard on roofs

Between summer UV, sudden hailstorms, and heavy winter snow load, a Treasure Valley roof works harder than most. We install architectural shingles rated for our climate and back every full replacement with a workmanship warranty that actually means something.

From the first free inspection to the final cleanup with our magnetic nail sweep, you deal with real people who live and work in this valley.

content:sidebar.heading: What to expect during your roof replacement
content:sidebar.subheading: A day-by-day walkthrough of a typical Peak Roofing Co install.
content:sidebar.body:
Before we start

Every project begins with a free, no-pressure inspection. We document the condition of your roof with photos, measure it precisely, and walk you through your options and financing — all before you sign anything.

Tear-off day

Our crew arrives early, protects your landscaping and siding, and strips the old roofing down to the deck.

Installation

We install ice-and-water shield, synthetic underlayment, and your chosen architectural shingles to GAF spec. Most Boise-area homes are completed in a single day.

Cleanup & final walkthrough

We run a magnetic sweep for stray nails, haul away every scrap, and do a final walkthrough with you before registering your warranty.

content:stat-interrupt.heading: Nearly two decades on Treasure Valley roofs
content:stat-interrupt.bodyTop: Peak Roofing Co isn't a storm-chaser passing through after the next big hail event. We're a local, licensed Idaho contractor with deep roots in Boise, Meridian, and Eagle — and the track record to prove it.
content:stat-interrupt.bodyBottom: Those numbers add up to something simple: when you hire Peak, you're hiring a crew that will still be here for the warranty.

content:quote-band.quote: I grew up in Boise, and I roof every house like it belongs to someone I'll run into at the grocery store — because usually it does.

content:qa.heading: Roof replacement questions, answered
content:qa.subheading: The things Boise homeowners ask us most before getting started.

items.question: Does my insurance cover a hail-damaged roof?
items.answer: Often, yes. If your roof was damaged in a covered storm, your homeowner's policy may pay for a full replacement minus your deductible.

items.question: How long does a typical replacement take?
items.answer: Most single-family homes in the Treasure Valley are completed in one day. Larger or steeper roofs may take two.

items.question: What warranty do you offer?
items.answer: Every full replacement includes our 10-year workmanship warranty on top of the manufacturer's shingle warranty.

items.question: Do you offer financing?
items.answer: Yes — we offer flexible monthly payment plans with quick approval.

items.title: Are you licensed and insured in Idaho?
items.body: Ask for the license number and a current certificate of insurance, not just a promise.

items.title: Is your workmanship warranty in writing?
items.body: Material warranties come from the manufacturer. The install warranty has to come from the roofer.

items.title: Will your own crew do the work?
items.body: Confirm whether they subcontract, and who is actually accountable on your roof.

items.title: Can I see local references and reviews?
items.body: Recent Treasure Valley jobs you can drive by beat a stock photo gallery.

items.title: Is the estimate itemized?
items.body: A real estimate breaks out tear-off, materials, labor, and cleanup.

items.title: Who handles my insurance claim?
items.body: A good roofer documents storm damage and works directly with your adjuster.

items.title: What happens if it leaks later?
items.body: You want a clear response time and a company that will still be here in five years.
